items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: We have been visiting with Mr. Louis Armstrong internationally known New Orleans jazz trumpeter and band leader and his guests Mr. Benny Benack and Dr. Frederick Dorian.

ctx.x: Great with life itself, and with our heritage. In this series of heritage programs, we are privileged to meet Mr. Louis Armstrong, the internationally known New Orleans jazz trumpeter and band leader. In this fourth program, Mr. Armstrong and his guests, Mr. Benny Benack, jazz trumpeter, band leader, and assistant director of the University of Pittsburgh Band, and Dr. Frederick Dorian, musicologist at Carnegie Institute of Technology and program annotator for the Pittsburgh Symphony, will discuss jazz is just…

A lot of people start breaking music down, and they say, this is good music, and that's bad, whether it's symphony or jazz. And actually, I think music is music, and I think there's a purpose for music. Maybe that's the thing. Maybe we shouldn't say it's good technically, or it's good this way, or structurally. Maybe there's a feeling we should get out of music. What do you think about it? You say, a lot of people that go in and do all that, they don't know anything about music. You understand?
